Terms.CommonMistake: Writing a huge unread GDD once, then never updating it as the game changes.
Terms.PracticePrompt: Create a two-page GDD covering pillars, core loop, and out-of-scope list.

Terms.ShortDefinition: A scheduled production checkpoint with concrete deliverables and review criteria.
Terms.SimpleExplanation: A dated goal that shows what must be playable or finished by then.
Terms.WhyItMatters: Milestones keep scope honest and create moments to course-correct.
Terms.Example: Alpha milestone requires all vertical-slice systems playable end to end.
Terms.CommonMistake: Setting date-only milestones with no acceptance criteria.
Terms.PracticePrompt: Write acceptance criteria for your next milestone in one checklist page.

Terms.ShortDefinition: Development phases where alpha proves incomplete systems and beta focuses on polish and scale.
Terms.SimpleExplanation: Alpha is still rough but playable; beta is closer to ship and needs wider testing.
Terms.WhyItMatters: Phase labels set expectations for content completeness and bug severity targets.
Terms.Example: Closed beta expands to thousands of players to validate servers and onboarding.
Terms.CommonMistake: Calling a feature-incomplete build beta to satisfy a calendar promise.
Terms.PracticePrompt: Define exit criteria that separate your alpha from beta for content and stability.

Terms.ShortDefinition: A build intended to ship if final verification finds no blocking issues.
Terms.SimpleExplanation: The almost-final package you will release unless a blocker appears.
Terms.WhyItMatters: RC discipline prevents late risky changes from destabilizing launch.
Terms.Example: RC1 passes certification smoke tests and waits on a final store screenshot update.
Terms.CommonMistake: Continuing to merge non-critical features into an RC branch.
Terms.PracticePrompt: Create an RC change policy listing what may and may not land after RC tag.

Terms.ShortDefinition: A structured review after a milestone or launch that captures what worked and what failed.
Terms.SimpleExplanation: A honest team meeting that turns recent pain into future process improvements.
Terms.WhyItMatters: Post-mortems convert expensive mistakes into institutional learning.
Terms.Example: After a rocky launch, the team documents root causes for crash triage delays.
Terms.CommonMistake: Blaming individuals instead of systems, handoffs, and missing safeguards.
Terms.PracticePrompt: Run a blameless post-mortem with timeline, root causes, and three action items.

Terms.ShortDefinition: Adapting text, audio, imagery, and cultural details for specific languages and regions.
Terms.SimpleExplanation: Preparing the game so players in other countries can understand and enjoy it.
Terms.WhyItMatters: Localization expands market reach and is often required for platform deals.
Terms.Example: UI, subtitles, and voice lines are adapted for five launch languages.
Terms.CommonMistake: Leaving localization until certification week with no string freeze.
Terms.PracticePrompt: Create a localization schedule with string freeze, translation, and LQA gates.

Terms.ShortDefinition: Mandatory technical and compliance testing by platform holders before store release.
Terms.SimpleExplanation: The official exam your build must pass to appear on a console or storefront.
Terms.WhyItMatters: Certification failures can delay launches by weeks if caught late.
Terms.Example: A console submission fails for improper suspend-resume handling and must be resubmitted.
Terms.CommonMistake: Treating TRC or store checks as optional until the final week.
Terms.PracticePrompt: Run an internal certification checklist two milestones before submission.

Terms.ShortDefinition: A partner that funds, markets, distributes, or certifies a game in exchange for commercial terms.
Terms.SimpleExplanation: The company that helps get your game funded, marketed, and onto platforms.
Terms.WhyItMatters: Publisher relationships shape milestones, creative approvals, and revenue shares.
Terms.Example: A publisher funds production and handles console submission while the studio focuses on gameplay.
Terms.CommonMistake: Signing terms without understanding milestone deliverables and kill criteria.
Terms.PracticePrompt: List five questions you would ask a publisher about creative control and recoupment.

Terms.ShortDefinition: A short, time-boxed development cycle with a committed set of deliverables.
Terms.SimpleExplanation: A one or two week work burst with a clear finish line.
Terms.WhyItMatters: Sprints create predictable planning cadence and frequent integration points.
Terms.Example: A two-week sprint delivers a new enemy type, related VFX, and automated tests.
Terms.CommonMistake: Overcommitting sprint scope and carrying unfinished work indefinitely.
Terms.PracticePrompt: Plan one sprint with capacity estimates and a demoable goal at the end.

Terms.ShortDefinition: Extended overtime used to meet deadlines, often signaling planning or scope failure.
Terms.SimpleExplanation: Working long extra hours because the schedule and scope no longer match.
Terms.WhyItMatters: Chronic crunch harms health, quality, and retention of experienced staff.
Terms.Example: A team works nights for three weeks to hit a publisher milestone.
Terms.CommonMistake: Normalizing crunch as culture instead of treating it as a planning emergency.
Terms.PracticePrompt: Identify one recurring crunch cause and propose a scope or staffing countermeasure.

Terms.ShortDefinition: Legal rights over creative assets, brands, code, and licenses used or created by a project.
Terms.SimpleExplanation: Who owns the characters, code, music, and brand names.
Terms.WhyItMatters: Clear IP ownership prevents legal blocks on shipping, sequels, and merchandising.
Terms.Example: A studio confirms music licenses allow gameplay streaming before launch marketing.
Terms.CommonMistake: Using unlicensed assets in a vertical slice that later cannot ship.
Terms.PracticePrompt: Inventory third-party assets and mark license constraints for commercial release.
